reading.thesis: Land Shabraz, keep him alive the turn he lands, and turn every card the deck draws into a +1/+1 counter on a flyer. Draw doublers and Lae'zel multiply the counters, and double strike cashes him in for 21 commander damage (stack 006); a damage doubler should do the same, but no stack has resolved it (open_questions[0]). Brallin is the second road, not the engine.

open_questions.question: Does Shabraz's combat damage under Gratuitous Violence (doubled) or Fiery Emancipation (tripled), and Brallin's combat damage with Torbran's +2, count in full as commander damage, and what size of double-striking Shabraz is lethal by commander damage under each?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The output stage's job toward the PRIMARY wincon rests on oracle text alone. Every passing amplifier stack (007, 011, 013) is about Brallin's or Needlehead's pings, not Shabraz in combat. The same question covers Torbran on Brallin's combat damage, which the wincon stage names as part of the second road; 005, 007 and 009 resolve only his noncombat pings.

open_questions.question: With Teferi's Ageless Insight (or Bard) out, how many counters does Shabraz get from one Wheel of Fortune, and with Lae'zel as well?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The conversion stage's two draw doublers are the core of the Shabraz-first rebuild, and no passing stack includes either one. The primary line (conversion -> wincon) is unverified.

open_questions.question: Does a draw on first-strike damage (Enduring Curiosity, Mask of Memory) add its counter to Shabraz before regular combat damage, the way Kitsa's activated loot does in stack 006? (Sokka draws on attack and Willie only on his own damage, so neither is in question.)
open_questions.why_it_matters: If so, every combat draw is a +1 or +2 on the second hit, and the double-strike kill needs a smaller Shabraz.

open_questions.question: How often is Shabraz on the battlefield and protected by turn five, and how often does he survive to attack the turn after he lands?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Ignition is one card and the brief has no measured rate for it. Every priced group is a proxy, and the goldfish has no removal, so survival is not something it can read.

open_questions.question: Is Brallin worth casting in the Shabraz-first list, or is he now a second commander you hold back, given that the discard engine (Glint-Horn, Psychosis Crawler, Needlehead, Rielle, loots) was cut?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The verified table kill (stack 009) still needs Brallin. The model files him as the second road, and whether that is real depends on how often he is cast.

findings.claim: double strike cashes him in for 21 commander damage (stack 006); a damage doubler should do the same, but no stack has resolved it (open_questions[0])
findings.note: Round-2 blocking finding resolved. The 21 now rests on stack 006 (double strike plus a Kitsa loot between strikes, a passing stack). The damage-doubler route is explicitly hedged and points to open_questions[0]. 'Draw doublers ... multiply the counters' has no stack behind it, but it is a direct oracle reading: Teferi's Ageless Insight and Bard replace one draw with two, and Shabraz triggers per card drawn. open_questions[1] asks only about the size of the effect. Not an over-claim.

findings.claim: It needs 40 discards, so at least 20 opponent draws. Only the five draw-seven wheels guarantee that: Wheel of Fortune, Reforge the Soul, Magus of the Wheel, Echo of Eons, Time Reversal ... Windfall on 009's board (opponent hands 4/3/2) gives 12, not a kill
findings.note: Round-2 blocking finding ('any wheel' scope) resolved. Re-derived: stack 009 starts with your hand empty. After a wheel, hand = 7 + 2N, where N is the number of opponent draws. Cleanup discards 2N, and Brallin deals 1 to EACH opponent per discard (cards.json oracle), so 2N >= 40 needs N >= 20. Three opponents drawing seven gives N = 21. The cards.json oracle confirms all five named wheels make each player draw seven. On 009's board Windfall uses the greatest number discarded, which is 4, so N = 12 (correct). Winds of Change and Jace's Archivist depend on hand sizes (correct). Will of the Jeskai is optional, and it draws only five (at most 15 opponent draws), so it cannot reach 20 even if every opponent accepts. The prose's 'lets opponents decline' is true but is the weaker of the two reasons. Collective Defiance targets one player (correct). 'No hand-size effect, and the 99 has none': I searched cards.json for 'maximum hand size' and got zero hits. This is mechanically checkable: a kill-threshold claim like 'needs N discards' could be recomputed from the cited stack's opponent life totals and per-discard damage.

v1_stages.label: PAY FIVE, THEN PAY FOR THE TURN
v1_stages.what_it_does: 38 lands and eleven accelerants (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, three Signets, three Talismans, Mind Stone, Fellwar Stone and Smothering Tithe) pay for a five-mana commander, then for protection or a wheel on the same turn. deck-audit puts the eleven-card ramp group in 57.4% of opening sevens and 67.0% by turn three, with a measured by-turn-six rate of 91.2% and mean turn 2.531. deck-facts: land sources R 31 / U 30 / W 22 against source targets R 48 / U 36 / W 22. Red is the colour that runs short, because Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation each cost three red pips, and 13 lands can enter tapped. Smothering Tithe is filed here for its Treasure. It also pays off every wheel, because each opponent draw is a Treasure they did not pay {2} for. Lands with a second job: Raugrin Triome cycles and Otawara channels, and both discards pay Brallin. Fiery Islet sacrifices for a draw, which pays Shabraz (oracle text).

v1_stages.label: SHABRAZ RESOLVES AND SURVIVES
v1_stages.what_it_does: Nothing in the deck is paid until Shabraz is on the battlefield. Every draw before that is just a card. He is a five-mana commander from the command zone, so the first window is turn four or five on the ramp above. The landing only counts if he is still there on your next turn. That is why this stage is one card and why the protection stage exists. Once he is out, every draw puts a +1/+1 counter on him and gains you 1 life (oracle text), with no further setup. Stacks 006, 008, 009 and 010 all start with him already on the battlefield, and none of them resolves the landing itself. The brief has no measured rate for when he is cast or how long he survives. The nearest priced proxy is the protection group: 8 cards, 45.6% of opening sevens, 54.7% by turn three, measured by-turn-six 86.9% (deck-audit). Brallin's partner trigger fetches Shabraz from the library only when Brallin enters; it is not standing recovery.

v1_stages.label: EVERY CARD DRAWN
v1_stages.what_it_does: Every draw is a counter and a life on Shabraz, so the deck's fuel is anything that draws. There are three shapes. (1) Standing engines that draw off the table: Rhystic Study, Esper Sentinel, Faerie Mastermind, Archmage Emeritus, Valeria Richards, plus Teferi, Master of Time's +1, which loots once on every player's turn. (2) Combat draws, which are three different triggers (oracle text). Enduring Curiosity and Mask of Memory fire when a creature deals combat damage to a player, so a double-striking Shabraz can trigger them on first-strike damage. Sokka draws when he and another creature attack, so his counter lands before any damage. Willie draws only when Willie himself connects. Whether a first-strike draw trigger grows Shabraz before regular damage is unverified (open_questions[2]); stack 006 resolved an activated loot in that step, not a trigger. (3) Burst: nine wheels (Wheel of Fortune, Windfall, Reforge the Soul, Echo of Eons, Time Reversal, Winds of Change, Will of the Jeskai, Magus of the Wheel, Jace's Archivist), Collective Defiance's one-sided wheel mode, Brainstorm, Prismari Command's draw-two, and Shark Typhoon's instant-speed cycling. Kitsa loots for {T}, and at power 3 or more she copies a wheel (stack 010). deck-audit's nine-card standing-draw group is in 49.8% of opening sevens, with a measured by-turn-six rate of 85.0%. The ten-card wheel group is in 53.7%, measured by turn six at 86.2%. The wheels and loots still discard, so Brallin is paid when he is out. Shuffle-wheels (Echo, Time Reversal, Winds of Change) do not trigger him. Will of the Jeskai does, when you choose to discard (oracle text).

v1_stages.label: ONE DRAW, SEVERAL COUNTERS
v1_stages.what_it_does: These are the multipliers between a draw and Shabraz's size. Teferi's Ageless Insight and Bard, King of Dale each turn every draw except the first draw-step draw into two (oracle text). Lae'zel turns each counter placement into one more counter. Consecrated Sphinx turns each opponent draw into two of yours, which makes a symmetrical wheel one-sided. Shang-Chi is a second draw-counter body that draws five more at its tenth counter, and those five pay Shabraz too. Stack 008: Windfall for seven with Lae'zel out leaves Shabraz 17/17. Stack 009: Wheel of Fortune under Sphinx gives 42 Sphinx draws on top of the seven, and Shabraz ends 52/52. The draw doublers and Shang-Chi are oracle-only here, because no passing stack resolves them. Lae'zel is a group of one in the declared targets, so deck-audit prices her alone: 7.1% of opening sevens, measured by turn six 22.2%. The stage as a whole has five cards and no tutor names them.

v1_stages.label: THE HIT, MULTIPLIED
v1_stages.what_it_does: The engine's product is a big commander, and these three cards multiply what he deals. Gratuitous Violence doubles damage from any creature you control. Fiery Emancipation triples damage from any source you control. Both apply to Shabraz's combat damage and to Brallin's pings (oracle text). Torbran adds 2 only to a RED source's damage to an opponent or their permanents, so he raises Brallin's pings and Brallin's combat damage but not Shabraz's, because Shabraz is white and blue. Stack 007: one Brallin ping under all three is at least 8 per opponent, and the damaged opponent orders the replacements. deck-audit's three-card amplifier group is in 19.9% of opening sevens and 25.1% by turn three, measured by turn six 53.6%. Each costs three red pips against a red-source shortfall (see mana). No passing stack resolves Shabraz's commander damage under Gratuitous Violence or Fiery Emancipation (open_questions).

v1_stages.label: COVER THE DAY HE LANDS
v1_stages.what_it_does: This stage keeps the ignition alive. Swiftfoot Boots gives standing hexproof and haste, so he can attack the turn he lands. Brotherhood Regalia equips a legendary for {1} and gives ward {2} and unblockable. The held instants are Shelter (protection from a colour, and it draws, so it pays Shabraz), Slip Out the Back (phases him out with a +1/+1 counter), Loran's Escape (hexproof and indestructible), Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat (both free with a commander out), and the counters Negate and Stubborn Denial. Stubborn Denial is a hard counter once Shabraz has 4 or more power. Grand Abolisher stops opponents casting any spell, and activating artifact, creature or enchantment abilities, on your turn, which covers the combat that cashes him in. It does not stop land or planeswalker abilities (oracle text). deck-audit's declared protection group (8 cards, including Akroma's Will, filed in wincon here) is in 45.6% of opening sevens and 54.7% by turn three, measured by turn six 86.9%, mean turn 3.087. The six-card answers group is in 36.4%. No passing stack in the current 99 resolves any of these protecting a commander. Stacks 004 and 005 hold Swiftfoot Boots in hand as wheel discard fodder; it never reaches the battlefield.

v1_stages.label: TWENTY-ONE IN ONE SWING
v1_stages.what_it_does: This is how the game ends: 21 commander damage, by double strike on a grown flyer. Fireshrieker (equip {2}) and Lizard Blades (reconfigure {2}) give double strike, and Blade Historian gives it to every attacker. Akroma's Will with a commander out gives both modes: double strike and flying, plus indestructible and protection from each colour for the swing. It is filed here rather than in protection because it is the only instant-speed double strike. Stack 006: Shabraz at 10/10 with Fireshrieker, plus a Kitsa loot between the strikes, deals 10 + 11 = 21. A draw trigger on first-strike damage (Enduring Curiosity, Mask of Memory) may do the same by oracle text; no stack resolves it (open_questions[2]). Brallin is the second road. He grows on discards; whether Torbran's +2 on his combat damage counts as commander damage is unresolved (open_questions[0]). Stack 009's table kill is his: the cleanup discard after a Sphinx wheel fires him 42 times into three 40-life opponents. In stack 009 the wheel discards an empty hand, so the kill is the cleanup discard alone. It needs 40 discards, so at least 20 opponent draws. Only the five draw-seven wheels guarantee that: Wheel of Fortune, Reforge the Soul, Magus of the Wheel, Echo of Eons, Time Reversal (the shuffle ones still serve, since the kill is the cleanup). Windfall on 009's board (opponent hands 4/3/2) gives 12, not a kill; Jace's Archivist and Winds of Change depend on hand sizes; Will of the Jeskai lets opponents decline; Collective Defiance hits one player. It also needs Sphinx, Brallin out, and no hand-size effect, and the 99 has none.

v1_map_disagreements.why: Draw sources are clustered on WHAT ELSE their text says, so the stage is spread across five cities. Standing engines that are creatures sit in Bodies. Three wheels on creatures or modal spells (Magus, Jace's Archivist, Collective Defiance) sit in Interaction. Mask of Memory and Esper Sentinel sit in Finishers. Brainstorm sits in Insurance. In this deck every one of them does the same job, a counter on Shabraz, and that job lives on the commander, not on the card. No card text can show it.

Equipment that protects (Swiftfoot Boots, Brotherhood Regalia) clusters with the equipment that kills (Fireshrieker, Lizard Blades) because the text shape is 'equipped creature has X'. Grand Abolisher clusters there too. The map files by delivery mechanism, and the engine files by what the card does for Shabraz.
Akroma's Will reads as a protection spell, and its double-strike mode is the one that ends games here. Brallin reads as a body. The map agrees on the equipment.
Torbran is a creature, so he clusters with bodies. The two enchantments that do the same replacement job sit in Finishers.
Two cities do one job. Ramp holds the rocks with fetches, Command Tower and the five-colour lands, and Mana holds the duals. That is a text split, not an engine split.
